parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Caller-generated key (e.g. a UUID v4) that makes a retried request safe (ADR-0027). Required on every POST: the service runs on Postgres in every deployment (ADR-0038) and rejects a request without it with 400 idempotency-key-required. Reuse the SAME key for retries of one logical request (same body) — the first response is stored and replayed byte-for-byte for the key's TTL (24h by default) when it is final for that request: a 2xx, a request-shape 400/422, or a FINAL conflict whose every operand the request itself carries (planned-heads-exceed-installed, planned-hours-exceed-capacity) — and a NEW key for each new logical request. A RETRYABLE refusal (404 resource-not-found or labour-plan-not-found, 400 unknown-path-id, the associate-state 409s, exceeds-installed-capacity, concurrent-modification) is NOT stored (ADR-0044): the key is released, so the same key and body executes again once the state allows it — and a different body under that key is a new request, not a 409. A 5xx answer is never stored: the request's writes and the key roll back, so a retry with the same key runs again. Reusing a key with a different request (method, path or body) is rejected with 409 idempotency-key-reused. A key that is not 1-128 printable ASCII characters that start and end with a visible character is a 400 idempotency-key-invalid. The pattern describes the header as sent on the wire (ADR-0042): the key itself (1-128 characters, visible first and last character), optionally followed by spaces or tabs. That trailing whitespace is HTTP optional whitespace (RFC 9112 field-line grammar): the HTTP stack drops it before the service reads the value (RFC 9110 section 5.5), so it is never part of the key. Leading whitespace is not in the pattern because HTTP clients do not send it. Every POST of this service takes the key; the key is global (looked up by key alone), so one key must never be reused across routes.
